record.paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Necessity of the assumptions in Fact 3.2
record.original_question: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and define the Bregman distance D(a, b) = f(a) - f(b) - <grad f(b), a - b> for b in U. Let C be a nonempty closed subset of U, let C* = grad f(C), and let U* = int dom f*. The set C is right D-Chebyshev when, for every x in U, the map P_right,C(x) = {y in C | D(x, y) = inf_{z in C} D(x, z)} is a singleton. If dom f = X, C* is contained in U*, and C is right D-Chebyshev, then C* is known to be convex. Are the full-domain assumption on f and the containment C* subset U* both genuinely necessary for that convexity conclusion?

evidence.quote: Definition 1.7 (Chebyshev sets) ... the set C is a right Chebyshev set with respect to the Bregman distance, or simply ->D-Chebyshev, if for every x in U, ->PC(x) is a singleton.
Fact 3.2 (->D-Chebyshev sets) (See [7, Theorem 7.3].) Suppose that dom f = X, that C* subseteq U*, and that C is ->D-Chebyshev. Then C* is convex.
Problem 2. Are the assumptions that f have full domain and that C* subseteq U* in Fact 3.2 really essential?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X=\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $f:X\to[-\infty,+\infty]$ be a convex Legendre function (i.e., $f$ is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, essentially smooth, and essentially strictly convex). Set $U=\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom} f$, and let $f^*$ be the Fenchel conjugate of $f$, with $U^*=\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom} f^*$. For $a\in X$ and $b\in U$ define the Bregman distance
$$D(a,b)=f(a)-f(b)-\langle \nabla f(b),\,a-b\rangle.$$
For a nonempty closed set $C\subseteq U$, set $C^*=\nabla f(C)$ and define the right Bregman projector
$$\overrightarrow{P}_C(x)=\{y\in C : D(x,y)=\inf_{z\in C}D(x,z)\},\qquad x\in U.$$
The set $C$ is said to be right $D$-Chebyshev if $\overrightarrow{P}_C(x)$ is a singleton for every $x\in U$.

It is known that if $\operatorname{dom} f=X$, $C^*\subseteq U^*$, and $C$ is right $D$-Chebyshev, then $C^*$ is convex.

Question: Are both hypotheses — namely that $f$ has full domain ($\operatorname{dom} f=X$) and that $C^*\subseteq U^*$ — genuinely essential for the conclusion that $C^*$ is convex? Equivalently, does there exist a counterexample to convexity of $C^*$ when one of these two assumptions is dropped?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work on right Bregman Chebyshev/Klee sets (e.g., Bauschke–Macklem–Wang and later "Bregman distances without coercive condition" extensions) revisits these hypotheses, but no source in the search clearly confirms that the necessity of the full-domain assumption together with $C^*\subseteq U^*$ has been settled. The status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Klee sets and Chebyshev centers for the right Bregman distance
status_evidence.snippet: Studies right Bregman Chebyshev/Klee sets under assumptions including full domain of f.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work continues to use these assumptions without proving them dispensable.

status_evidence.title: Bregman distances without coercive condition: suns, Chebyshev sets and Klee sets
status_evidence.snippet: Extends results on Chebyshev/Klee sets to settings without coercivity.
status_evidence.claim: Some assumptions have been weakened, but necessity of the specific pair (full domain and C*⊆U*) is not confirmed resolved.
